title: There's a Crystal Vibrating 32,768 Times a Second in Your Watch

segments.text: There's a crystal inside your watch, shaking thousands of times every second.
In nineteen twenty-seven, engineers at Bell Labs found it. Quartz.
Run electricity through it, and it vibrates at a perfectly steady rate.
In your watch, thirty-two thousand, seven hundred and sixty-eight times a second. The watch just counts.
The first quartz wristwatch cost about as much as a small car.
But scientists wanted something even steadier. Atoms.
Today, one second is officially nine billion, one hundred ninety-two million, six hundred thirty-one thousand, seven hundred and seventy ticks of a caesium atom.
The best clocks lose less than one second in a hundred million years.
Every GPS satellite carries atomic clocks. Off by a millionth of a second, and your map misses by hundreds of metres.
Your phone checks those clocks all day. That's how it always knows the time.
